summary: Defines a registry for profile URIs to be used in specifications that standardize profiles.

plainLanguage.summary: A profile is a small extra set of rules for a data format. This sets up a list where those profile names are officially recorded.

subtitle: An IANA registry for profile URIs used in Internet protocols and data formats.

tldr.problem: As specifications use profile URIs to signal support for additional semantics (constraints, extensions, conventions), these URIs are created independently, making it hard to ensure interoperability and manage the landscape.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7284 establishes an IANA registry where profile URIs can be formally registered with a common name, description, and reference, similar to how media types and link relations are managed.
tldr.outcome: This registry provides a central place to discover and coordinate profile identifiers, allowing independent clients and servers to couple to standard contracts rather than to each other.

today: RFC 7284 is an Internet Standard. The Profile URI registry remains active at IANA and is used in specifications that standardize profiles, providing a centralized place to manage and discover profile identifiers.

sections.title: What Are Profiles?
sections.content:
As defined in RFC 6906, a profile is a way to add extra semantics to a data format without changing the basic format itself. Profiles can signal support for constraints, conventions, extensions, or any other aspects that do not alter the fundamental meaning of the format. Each profile is identified by a URI.

Because profiles are identified by URI, anyone can create them independently without central coordination. However, this can lead to fragmentation and make it harder for clients and servers to discover standard profiles or ensure they are using compatible profiles.
sections.plainLanguage: A profile is like a special flavor of a standard format. Instead of making a whole new format, you keep the format the same but add extra rules. Each flavor has its own web address.

sections.title: The Registry and Registration Process
sections.content:
RFC 7284 establishes the "Profile URIs" registry at IANA. To be registered, a profile URI must be documented in a permanent, publicly available specification in sufficient detail for interoperable implementation.

The registration template requires a profile URI, a common name, a description, and optionally a reference. Registrations are accepted on a "First Come First Served" basis. Initial registry contents include the exemplary profile urn:example:profile-uri, Dublin Core HTML metadata, and three JSON-LD profiles (expanded, compacted, and flattened forms).
sections.plainLanguage: To register a profile, you fill out a form with the web address, a name, a description, and a link to the documentation. IANA keeps the list on a first-come-first-served basis.

sections.title: Benefits and Use
sections.content:
Similar to media types and link relation types, a central registry for profile URIs allows independent evolution of clients and servers: both couple to standard profile contracts rather than directly to each other. This decoupling reduces complexity and increases interoperability.

The registry also reduces the chance of collisions and makes it easier for implementers to discover and reuse existing profiles rather than creating new ones unnecessarily. It mirrors the successful IANA approach for other naming systems.
sections.plainLanguage: Having an official list means clients and servers do not have to know about each other; they both just know the profile names from the official list. This makes it easier to build compatible systems.
